spatial_claims.claim: ABCD is a square with all sides equal (AB = BC = CD = DA) and all four angles are right angles
E is the intersection point of diagonals AC and BD, lying inside the square
DA is parallel to CB (co-interior angles DAB and ABC sum to two right angles)
AB is parallel to DC (co-interior angles ABC and BCD sum to two right angles)
angle ABE = angle CDE (alternate interior angles with AB parallel to DC, transversal BD)
angle BAE = angle DCE (alternate interior angles with AB parallel to DC, transversal AC)
AE = CE (from congruence of triangles AEB and CED); E is midpoint of diagonal AC
BE = DE (from congruence of triangles AEB and CED); E is midpoint of diagonal BD
angle AEB = angle AED (from congruence of triangles AEB and AED)
E lies on line BD, so angles AEB and AED are supplementary (on one side of line BD at point E)
angle AEB = angle AED = one right angle (supplementary and equal)
Ray AE falls between rays AB and AD, so angle BAD = angle EAB + angle EAD (angle decomposition)
angle EAB = angle EAD (from Step 6 congruence), each equals half a right angle
AE = BE (triangle AEB is isosceles with equal base angles)
EA = EB = EC = ED; all four vertices equidistant from E
Circle centered at E with radius EA passes through all four vertices A, B, C, D

configuration_map: Point E is the intersection of diagonals AC and BD of square ABCD. It lies inside the square on both diagonals. Throughout the proof, E is consistently treated as: (1) a point on segment BD, enabling the supplementary angle argument in Step 7; (2) the midpoint of both diagonals (AE = CE, BE = DE from Step 5); (3) a point in the interior of angle BAD at vertex A, enabling the angle decomposition in Step 8; (4) equidistant from all four vertices (Step 12), making it the center of the circumscribed circle. All these properties are mutually consistent for the center of a square.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The central construction point E at the intersection of the diagonals is used consistently throughout: it lies on both diagonals (enabling midpoint and supplementary angle arguments), it is inside the square (enabling valid angle decompositions at each vertex), and it is equidistant from all vertices. The one angle decomposition (Step 8: angle BAD = angle EAB + angle EAD) is valid because ray AE from vertex A into the square interior falls between rays AB and AD. No pairwise contradiction exists between any spatial claims.
